tools.name: wenmar_vin
tools.description: Decode vehicle identification numbers into year, make, model, trim, generation, engine (with horsepower, valve train and fuel injection), drivetrain, brakes, battery and charging, safety equipment, lights and keyless ignition, the manufacturer's notes, every NHTSA attribute with its source, and the matching catalog entry. year_conclusive=false means the VIN leaves the model year open: check the vehicle's label. action=decode takes `vin` (and optionally `year` to override the model year). action=batch takes `vins`, at most 50, and returns one result per VIN in order. A wrong check digit is not an error: the result has valid=false and a warning. action=overview takes `vin` (and optionally `year`) and gives everything held for the model year the VIN decodes to in one answer: the decode in brief, a count of the recall campaigns that may apply to that year, make and model with the three newest, and links. A block with no data is null. action=fuel, specs, fluids or tires takes `vin` (and optionally `year`) and gives that data for the model year the VIN decodes to: fuel consumption ratings from EPA and Natural Resources Canada (optional `country`, us or ca), specifications from EPA's files, fluids (the engine oil grade EPA records, and records a person read from the maker's own documents, each with its source and the day it was checked), or the original-equipment tire fitments. When the decode settles the engine, fuel, specs and fluids hold only what is for that engine and `engine_settled` is true; tires are never narrowed.

country.description: For action=fuel: us for EPA's ratings, ca for Natural Resources Canada's. Leave out for both.

vin.description: A 17-character VIN. Spaces and dashes are ignored.

year.description: Model year to use instead of the one worked out from the VIN.

tools.name: wenmar_vehicles
tools.description: Look up vehicles by year, make, model, submodel and engine. Actions: years; makes (optional `year`); models (`make`, optional `year`); submodels (`make`, `model`, `year`); engines (`make`, `model`, `year`, optional `submodel`); search (`query`, such as "2019 civic si" or "chevy 1500"); entry (`id`, such as "2019_honda_civic_si"); overview (`id`: everything held for that model year in one answer, with a count of the recall campaigns that may apply and the three newest; a block with no data is null); model_years (`make`, `model`: every model year of one model, newest first, each with its vehicle id and the number of recall campaigns that may apply); safety (`id`: NHTSA's crash test ratings for that model year, one entry for each vehicle NHTSA rated, by body style and drive, each with its stars; an entry with no stars is a vehicle NHTSA lists and has not tested); fuel (`id`, optional `country` us or ca: fuel consumption ratings from EPA and Natural Resources Canada, each saying in `confidence` how far it was matched: model, engine or submodel); specs (`id`: transmission, drive, recommended fuel and more from EPA's files, one entry per EPA rating); fluids (`id`: the engine oil grade EPA records for each engine, and records a person read from the maker's own documents, each with its `source` and the day it was `checked`; an empty list means nobody has recorded it); tires (`id`: every original-equipment tire size on record with the trims it covers; none is picked). `make` and `model` take a name, an alias or an id. `term` narrows a list to names starting with it. `scope` is light (cars, MPVs and trucks; the default), all, or a vPIC vehicle type id. action=complaints takes `id` and gives what owners reported to NHTSA about that model year as counts by component, with the median mileage owners gave: these are owners' reports, not verified, and a count is not a rate.

country.description: For action=fuel: us or ca. Leave out for both.

tools.name: wenmar_recalls
tools.description: Recall campaigns from NHTSA (United States) and Transport Canada that may apply to a vehicle. A campaign lists a year, a make and a model, so every answer has may_apply: true. It may apply; confirm by VIN with the manufacturer, or at the addresses in `lookup`. This is never a lookup by VIN. action=vehicle takes `id`, a vehicle id such as "2018_ford_f-150". action=vin takes `vin` (and optionally `year`): it decodes the VIN and lists the recalls of its model year. action=campaign takes `source` (nhtsa or tc) and `campaign`, such as "19V888000", and gives that campaign with every vehicle it lists. action=search lists campaigns newest first, narrowed by any of `make`, `model` (needs `make`), `year`, `component` and `query` (free text); `limit` is at most 100 and 25 when left out; `cursor` is `next_cursor` of the page before. action=recent takes `since`, a day such as "2026-09-01", and lists the campaigns reported on or after it, newest first, each with the vehicles it lists; it also takes `make`, `limit` and `cursor`. `country` is us or ca on every action but campaign; left out, both.

since.description: For recent: a day, such as 2026-09-01. Campaigns reported on or after it are listed.

vin.description: A 17-character VIN. Spaces and dashes are ignored.

year.description: For vin: the model year to use. For search: only campaigns that list this model year.

tools.name: wenmar_bulletins
tools.description: Manufacturer communications NHTSA publishes: service bulletins, service campaigns, warranty extensions and over-the-air updates. Each has NHTSA's summary, the manufacturer's own document number, and `document`, the address NHTSA's copy of the document is expected at (not confirmed; null for old ones). The document itself is the manufacturer's and is not returned. A bulletin lists model years: it is not a recall and does not say a vehicle is affected. action=vehicle takes `id`, a vehicle id such as "2018_ford_f-150", and gives one page of that model year's bulletins, newest first, with `counts` by type, component, trouble code and topic. action=vin takes `vin` (and optionally `year`) and does the same for the model year the VIN decodes to. action=get takes `nhtsa_id` and gives one bulletin with every vehicle it lists. action=search lists all bulletins newest first, narrowed by `make`, `model` (needs `make`) and `year`. Every action but get takes `type` (service_bulletin, service_campaign, warranty_extension, over_the_air, emissions, other), `component` (an id from `counts.components`, such as brakes), `code` (a trouble code such as P0420), `topic` (maintenance), `query` (free text in the summary, such as a symptom), `limit` (at most 100, 25 when left out) and `cursor` (`next_cursor` of the page before). This tool needs the hosted service: a local data file does not hold bulletins.

nhtsa_id.description: NHTSA's id number for the communication.

vin.description: A 17-character VIN. Spaces and dashes are ignored.

year.description: For vin: the model year to use. For search: only bulletins that list this model year.

tools.name: wenmar_codes
tools.description: Generic OBD-II trouble codes, described in Wenmar Open's own words: a title, what the code means, common causes, first checks, the components it concerns and related codes. Only codes every maker uses the same way are described (P0, P2, P3400 and up, B0, C0, U0, U3). Manufacturer-specific codes are not described. action=get takes `code`, such as "P0420", and gives its description. action=search lists the described codes by code, narrowed by `query` (text in the code, title or meaning) and `system` (powertrain, body, chassis, network, or an area such as powertrain/emissions); pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor`. action=vehicle takes `id`, a vehicle id such as "2018_ford_f-150", and `code`, any code, a manufacturer-specific one included: it gives the description (null when there is none), the bulletins of that model year whose NHTSA summary names the code, and the bulletins and recalls of that model year about the same components. A part of that answer is null where the data is not held. A description is general and is not a diagnosis; a bulletin or recall listed may apply to the model year and is not confirmed for one vehicle.

code.description: A trouble code, such as P0420. Either case.

tools.name: wenmar_payroll_deductions
tools.description: Works out the deductions from one regular pay in Ontario by CRA's T4127 formulas (Option 1): federal and Ontario income tax, CPP, CPP2 and EI, the net pay, the employer's CPP, CPP2 and EI, and every T4127 factor used with what it means. Takes `frequency` (weekly, biweekly, semi-monthly or monthly) and `gross`, the gross pay for the period. `federal_claim` and `provincial_claim` are the TD1 claim amounts: left out, each is the basic personal amount (claim code 1), and 0 is claim code 0. `pay_date` (YYYY-MM-DD) chooses the tables; left out, it is today, and a day outside the tables held is an error that names their dates. `ytd_cpp`, `ytd_cpp2`, `ytd_ei` and `ytd_pensionable` are what was deducted and earned on earlier pays this calendar year. Money is a number or text such as "2400.00". Ontario only; not for a bonus, commission or retroactive pay. The answer is an estimate and the employer remains liable to CRA for what it deducts and remits: say so, and point to CRA's Payroll Deductions Online Calculator at `pdoc_url`.

federal_claim.description: Federal TD1 claim amount. Left out: claim code 1.

gross.description: Gross pay for one pay period, in dollars.

province.description: Ontario only for now. Left out: ON.

provincial_claim.description: Ontario TD1ON claim amount. Left out: claim code 1.

ytd_cpp.description: CPP (base and first additional) deducted earlier this year.
